summary: SSE chat: intermittent quiet-gap then early connection close under burst traffic (clients see incomplete finalization)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that server-sent events (SSE) chat sessions intermittently experience a quiet gap (10-30s of no data) after initial tokens are streamed, followed by premature connection close without a final DONE/END token. Clients observe incomplete finalization and retry logic is triggered. Impact: Helios AI reports 12% of sessions in the last 6 hours ended without finalization, affecting live chat user experience and causing their client-side retrys and duplicate messages. Environment: Production us-east, dedicated pool for Helios (reserved capacity). Observed across multiple app versions and both SSE and websocket clients behind the same corporate proxy chain.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Helios integration keys with dedicated pool in us-east. 2) Start a streaming chat request via SSE with system + user prompt ~1200 tokens. 3) Under burst load (10 parallel streams per connection) send 40 concurrent requests from single IP subnet. 4) Observe initial token chunks arrive, then silence for 10-30s, then connection closed by server (client sees connection closed code 1006 or HTTP/1.1 200 then connection tear down).
logs:
- Sample request id: req-hippo-20260310-9a3b (logged at edge-proxy 2026-03-10T14:18:02Z)
- Edge proxy logs: 'upstream write timeout after 30s' for several connections.
- Serving runtime traces: request req-hippo-20260310-9a3b attached to worker rtm-22; last recorded token emission at 2026-03-10T14:18:06Z, worker heartbeat continues until 2026-03-10T14:18:39Z.
- Metrics: 502 spike and connection reset counts aligned with CPU scheduling jitter and host-level OOM kills on one host in the dedicated pool (host-11).
- Client side: Chrome SSE client reports 'EventSource failed to connect' only after connection close; some WebSocket clients show '1006 abnormal closure'.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: (A) Edge-proxy or upstream timeout kills connection during temporary worker stall. (B) Worker is emitting tokens but edge-proxy coalesces or stalls chunked transfer due to connection backpressure. (C) Dedicated host experiencing transient CPU/GPU scheduling leading to delayed token emission and proxy-level timeout. Findings so far: - Correlated quiet gaps with host-11 CPU steal and a kernel IO wait spike at 14:18:30Z. - Worker rtm-22 continued to produce tokens (application logs show generated token buffers) but net bytes on socket did not increase during quiet window. - Proxy (envoy fork) reports upstream send buffer full and applied a 30s write timeout for a subset of connections. - Not all hosts in the pool show the pattern; 3 of 12 hosts had elevated steal/IO waits. - No model-level exception or OOM recorded in runtime logs. - Similar but not identical symptom to SUP-124309 (proxy coalescing) but here gaps are longer and accompanied by host-level resource contention. Working theory: transient host-level contention delays runtime's ability to flush socket buffers while proxy enforces write timeouts leading to orderly or abrupt connection tear-down.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer posted timeline and sample request ids. They see ~12% failure rate during 13:00-15:00 window.
Priya Nair (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced in staging with synthetic burst; observed proxy upstream write-timeout at 30s. Opened edge-proxy investigation.

Arjun Patel (Serving Runtime) 2026-03-11: Added extra logging around socket flush and token emission. No runtime exceptions seen; token buffers ready but syscall write returns EAGAIN during quiet window.

Katrina Lopez (Customer Success) 2026-03-11: Notified Helios with temporary mitigation suggestion to lower client-side request parallelism and extend client reconnect timeout to 45s. Helios will try throttles on their side and report back.
Priya Nair (SRE) 2026-03-12: Rolled a hotfix to edge-proxy to increase upstream write-timeout from 30s to 60s for dedicated-pool routes as a temporary mitigation; monitoring for retry amplification.
resolution: Mitigation applied: edge-proxy timeout increased to 60s for affected dedicated pool; ops drained and reprovisioned 3 hosts with high CPU steal. Customer advised to reduce client parallelism as short-term workaround. Next steps: 1) Implement non-blocking socket flush improvements in serving runtime to avoid long syscall backpressure (PR opened). 2) Add host-level anomaly detector for CPU steal/IO wait for dedicated pools. 3) Follow-up on edge-proxy flow-control logic to avoid coalescing chunks. Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/318, https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming/pull/904. Target resolution date: 2026-03-18.
